title: In blind tests, top violinists often couldn’t pick out a Stradivarius
body: Violins made by Antonio Stradivari around three centuries ago sell for millions and are widely believed to have an unmatched sound. But in double-blind studies published in 2012 and 2014, experienced violinists wearing modified goggles could not reliably tell top old Italian violins from good new ones, and many preferred the new. Researchers still debate what makes a great violin, but the old-instrument edge seems smaller than the legend.

slides.question: How were the violinists kept from seeing which instrument they played?
